data.narrative:
MacroFab is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $141M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and Nimble Robotics), supplemented by reference to a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $141M total raised as a baseline and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $240M. The peer-median method examines five robotics companies at Series B, C, and D stages, identifying a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. This wider band reflects stage and growth-profile variation within the peer cohort, with Hadrian and Nimble Robotics both at Series C valued at $1.6B and $1.0B respectively.

The triangulated analysis yields a range of $204M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $945M. The substantial spread reflects tension between MacroFab's capital-raised position and the valuation multiples observed in comparable-stage robotics companies. Key uncertainties include revenue, unit economics, and customer concentration relative to named peers—none of which are present in available data. A narrower range would require disclosure of operational metrics or revenue multiples by which to calibrate peer comparability.
